cases.title: Fix `pMap` hanging on a source that blocks in `next()` after it is exhausted
cases.purpose: Map an iterable through asynchronous work with configured concurrency and ordered results.
cases.public_docs:
Module: await load('./index.js'); default export pMap, named exports pMapIterable and pMapSkip.
pMap(input, mapper, options?) returns a Promise of mapped values in input order. Inputs may be synchronous or asynchronous iterables and contain values or promises. Mapper receives (resolvedValue, inputIndex), and may return a value or promise. concurrency is an integer >=1 or Infinity (default Infinity). Empty input yields []. Returning pMapSkip omits that item. With stopOnError=true (default), an input or mapper rejection rejects the result; false waits for mapper work and aggregates mapper errors. A supplied AbortSignal cancels the operation using its reason.
pMapIterable(input, mapper, options?) returns an async iterable yielding mapped values in input order. concurrency bounds simultaneous mapper work; backpressure (default concurrency) bounds buffered results and must be >=concurrency. Mapper receives the resolved value and its input index. Mapper failures propagate to the consumer. pMapSkip omits an item.
Keep iteration, error propagation, ordering, and configured work limits consistent for ordinary values, promise inputs, and async sources.

cases.title: Fix: Handle input rejections when already aborted (#46)
cases.purpose: Decorate a promise with timeout, fallback, and cancellation behavior.
cases.public_docs:
Module: await load('./index.js'); default export pTimeout, named export TimeoutError.
pTimeout(inputPromise, options) returns a decorated promise with .clear() to cancel its timeout. milliseconds is a positive number; Infinity disables timeout. Before timeout, it adopts the input fulfillment or rejection. When timeout expires, default behavior rejects with TimeoutError; message may be a string, an Error to reject with, or false to resolve undefined. A fallback function can provide a value/promise instead, and exceptions from fallback reject the decorated promise. Cancelable input promises have their .cancel() method called on ordinary timeout.
customTimers supplies {setTimeout, clearTimeout} for controlled timing. The functions follow timer callback/delay and timer-handle conventions. A supplied AbortSignal cancels using its reason, including when already aborted. Settled operations clean up active timers and abort listeners. The input remains a promise whose rejection must be handled.

cases.title: Fix the promise not fulfilling if the count is unachievable (#5)
cases.purpose: Collect the first requested number of eligible fulfilled input values.
cases.public_docs:
Module: await load('./index.js'); default export pSome (CommonJS), with pSome.AggregateError.
pSome(input, {count, filter?}) returns a cancelable Promise. input is an iterable of promises or ordinary values. It fulfills once count eligible values have fulfilled, with an array in fulfillment order. count is a finite number with minimum 1 and cannot exceed the number of input items. The optional synchronous filter(value) determines whether a fulfilled value is eligible; omitted filter accepts all values. If count becomes impossible, the operation rejects rather than waiting indefinitely. Rejected input errors are represented by AggregateError. Inputs that are still pending and have a .cancel() method are canceled when the operation settles; calling .cancel() on the result cancels pending inputs too.

cases.title: Fix missing `range()` in `createWithTimers()` return value & require Node.js 10 (#55)
cases.purpose: Create controllable promise delays with optional values, ranges, rejection, and cancellation.
cases.public_docs:
Module: await load('./index.js'); default export delay (CommonJS).
delay(milliseconds, {value?, signal?}?) creates a promise resolving after the delay with value. delay.reject(milliseconds, options?) rejects with the supplied value after the delay. delay.range(minimum, maximum, options?) resolves after a random integer number of milliseconds in the inclusive range, using the same value and signal options. Returned delay promises have .clear(), which cancels the timer and settles immediately according to the selected resolve/reject operation. An aborted signal rejects with an Error named AbortError.
delay.createWithTimers({setTimeout, clearTimeout}) creates an independent delay instance using the supplied timer functions. This instance provides the delay operations with the same API. Timers receive (callback, milliseconds), return a handle, and clearTimeout receives that handle.
